data.gender_notes: Prabir is used as a male name in Hindu naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: The name Prabir is derived from the Sanskrit word 'prabhR' which means 'bright' or 'shining one'. This name is often given to babies born in Hindu families as a symbol of wisdom, intelligence, and the divine light of knowledge. The name Prabir carries the meaning “Bright, Shining One” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Hindu tradition and is also used in Sanskrit, Bengali. Parents who choose Prabir usually hope their child will grow to embody bright, shining one and live with faith, good character and purpose.

historical_references.reference: Prabir Chandra Pal was a prominent leader of the Indian National Congress and a key figure in the Swadeshi Movement, which arose in response to the British government's imposition of new taxes on Indian goods in 1905. He was born on October 15, 1875, in Calcutta, India.

Another notable figure with the name Prabir was Prabir Shastri, an ancient Indian sage and poet who lived around 800 BC during the Gupta Empire. He is best known for his work 'Sabarasataka', a collection of 150 poems in the Bengali language.
